observations.text: SP, due to insufficient familiarity with the standby instrument presentation, could not fly the GCA final approach without assistance, and altitude deviation until on final exceeded 300 feet before the corrections were directed. Performance met the desired code for this stage, but at its lower edge, since the IP also executed part of the descent to MDA. Marginal performance for the Training Section - an independent standby instrument cross-check is expected to develop with the next exposures.

SP, on an early exposure to the approach on standby instruments, completed the GCA final approach with the IP's verbal prompts only, without the IP taking the controls. Altitude until on final was contained at 300 feet and heading at 10 degrees from the controller's assigned values, the deviations being recognized and corrected after the prompts. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained the cross-check of the standby attitude indicator, altimeter and airspeed indicator and flew the GCA final approach without IP prompts, holding altitude until on final within 200 feet, heading within 7 degrees and airspeed within +15 knots of the final approach speed. The minor deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the standby instruments approach with an accurate and rapid cross-check of the standby instruments, complying with all controller instructions and with the published routing and altitude restrictions. Altitude until on final was held within 150 feet, heading within 5 degrees and airspeed within +10/-5 knots, with the glide path kept only slightly above or slightly below throughout the final. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the standby instruments approach to the published GCA procedure without any IP intervention, with an uninterrupted scan and an immediate response to every controller correction. Deviations in altitude, heading and final approach speed were negligible throughout the final approach, and the glide path was flown without measurable excursion down to decision height. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized transition to the standby instruments, did not establish a usable cross-check between the standby attitude indicator and the standby altimeter and could not fly the GCA final approach without assistance. Altitude deviation until on final exceeded 300 feet and heading exceeded 10 degrees, with the result that the IP directed the corrections and executed part of the descent. Further practice in the raw standby instrument scan is required.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, left the standby instrument cross-check interrupted while working the controller's headings and did not maintain the final approach parameters without assistance. Airspeed decayed more than 10 knots below the final approach speed and altitude until on final exceeded 300 feet, with the result that the IP took the controls to re-establish the approach. The developing deviation was not recognized before the IP's intervention.

SP flew the GCA approach on standby instruments to the desired standard for this stage, completing the final approach after the IP's verbal prompts on heading and altitude. Deviations reached 300 feet in altitude until on final and 10 degrees in heading, that is at the limit of the desired code, and were recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier self-detection of the standby instrument deviations is expected on the following sortie.

SP flew the standby instruments approach with a maintained cross-check and without IP prompts, holding altitude until on final within 200 feet, heading within 7 degrees and airspeed within +15 knots of the final approach speed. All deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner and the controller's instructions were complied with without delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the standby instruments approach accurately and rapidly, complying with all ATC and controller instructions and respecting the published routing and altitude restrictions. Altitude until on final was held within 150 feet, heading within 5 degrees and airspeed within +10/-5 knots, and altitude at MDA was never below the published minimum and no more than 100 feet above it. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the GCA approach on standby instruments with an uninterrupted scan of the standby attitude indicator, altimeter, airspeed indicator and magnetic compass, anticipating each controller correction. Altitude, heading and airspeed deviations were negligible throughout and the approach was flown to MDA without a single prompt from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a scan pattern that dwelt on the standby attitude indicator, did not integrate the standby altimeter and airspeed indicator into the cross-check during the GCA final approach. Altitude until on final departed by more than 300 feet and airspeed fell more than 10 knots below the final approach speed, with the result that the IP directed the recovery and flew part of the approach. The published descent could not be completed without assistance.

SP, due to a false attitude perception that was not resolved against the instruments once the primary display was removed, did not maintain the briefed final approach attitude on the standby indicator. Heading diverged more than 10 degrees from the controller's assigned heading and altitude deviation until on final exceeded 300 feet, with the result that the IP assumed control to re-establish the approach. The undesired aircraft state was not recognized by the SP before the intervention.

SP, due to late and oversized corrections on the standby altimeter, did not stabilize the rate of descent during the GCA final approach on standby instruments. Altitude deviation until on final reached 300 feet and heading reached 10 degrees, corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. The approach was completed without the IP taking control, but recognition and correction were delayed.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained on the controller's continuous guidance calls, did not monitor the standby airspeed indicator during the final approach. Airspeed reached +20 knots above the final approach speed and altitude at MDA settled 200 feet above the published minimum, both being corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition and correction of the deviations occurred with delay.

SP flew the standby instruments approach within the desired standards, maintaining the cross-check and completing the final approach without the IP's intervention. However, altitude until on final twice reached 200 feet from the assigned value and heading 7 degrees, the corrections being applied in a timely manner but with more control activity than the profile required. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter altitude and heading control on standby instruments is expected to improve over the remaining sorties.

SP executed the standby instruments GCA approach flawlessly according to the standardized procedure, without mistakes and without the IP's intervention. Altitude until on final was held within 150 feet, heading within 5 degrees and airspeed within +10/-5 knots, with the glide path kept only slightly above or slightly below throughout the final. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the standby instruments approach with exceptional accuracy, transitioning to the standby attitude indicator immediately and maintaining a continuous cross-check under the reduced instrument presentation. Deviations from the assigned altitude, heading and final approach speed were negligible and the glide path was held without measurable excursion down to decision height. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized configuration sequence that left the aircraft fast at glide path intercept, did not establish the descent on the standby instruments at the controller's call. Altitude until on final departed by more than 300 feet and airspeed exceeded the final approach speed by more than 20 knots, with the result that the IP executed part of the approach to regain the profile. The approach could not be completed without assistance.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with aircraft control, communication and the standby instrument scan attempted simultaneously, did not maintain the parameters of the GCA final approach. Heading diverged more than 10 degrees from the controller's assigned heading and the aircraft descended below MDA, with the result that the IP intervened on the controls and directed the go-around. The developing undesired aircraft state was not recognized by the SP.

SP, due to a scan that fixated on the standby altimeter during the descent, did not hold the assigned heading through the controller's corrections on final. Heading deviation reached 10 degrees and altitude until on final reached 300 feet, corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. The approach was completed without the IP taking control, but the errors were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to absent inquiry when the observed aircraft performance did not match the expected after the primary display was removed, continued the final approach without reassessing the standby altimeter indication against the controller's advisory altitudes. Altitude at MDA was held 200 feet above the published minimum and airspeed reached +20 knots above the final approach speed, both corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to slightly delayed power corrections after gear and flap extension, did not hold the final approach speed constant during the standby instruments approach. Airspeed reached +15 knots above the final approach speed and altitude until on final 200 feet from the assigned value. Both deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on final, briefly interrupted the standby instrument cross-check during the descent on the GCA. Heading deviated 7 degrees from the controller's assigned heading and altitude until on final 200 feet, with the glide path allowed to go high before the correction was applied. The errors were self-detected and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention.

SP executed the standby instruments approach accurately and with sufficiency, complying with the controller's instructions and completing the approach without the IP's intervention. Altitude until on final and heading remained within 150 feet and 5 degrees respectively, but airspeed was twice allowed to reach the upper edge of the +10 knot tolerance before correction. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a steadier final approach speed on standby instruments is expected on the check ride.

SP flew the standby instruments GCA approach with exceptional accuracy under the degraded instrument presentation, maintaining an uninterrupted cross-check and anticipating every controller correction. Deviations in altitude, heading and final approach speed were negligible, the glide path was flown without measurable excursion and altitude at MDA was held at the published minimum. Above end of block MIF achieved.
